comments.body: Spiked 2026-10-26 on 0.19.0 with Claude Code 2.1.310, in panes started with `extras/claude-code/messaging-hooks.json`. Mid-turn and Stop delivery worked, but three problems would come with making the hooks the default: a_2pOSx27ml (a subagent's tool call takes the pane's message), a_2pOTIVxnx (a closed pane's session stays exiting while its Stop hook's wait runs), and a_2pOTJDMPl (a mid-turn message reaches the agent twice).

comments.body: 2026-11-10: rewritten to the design agreed with the owner (plugin PostToolUse hook for every session, no Stop hook, doorbell for idle agents) and moved to backlog-hi. The questions above are answered in the description.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Ship the messaging `PostToolUse` hook in every harness's plugin, so an agent that is running gets its messages at its next tool call without anything typed into its pane. An idle agent keeps getting the doorbell. Drop the `Stop` hook.

Decided with the owner, 2026-11-10. Originally from his Chat Notes, 2026-10-14: "mechanism for messaging between agents which doesn't just enter thru pane, since that can be blocked or occupied."

## Why

Today the doorbell types into the prompt, and it also types urgent posts into a busy prompt. That costs a two-step write so that a Return cannot land on a permission dialog, and the post waits while a dialog covers the prompt. `muster msg read --if-unread --from-hook` after each tool call hands the model the text with no typing at all. A hook that finds nothing exits 0 with no output, so Claude Code puts nothing into the context. The caller only sees a message when one has arrived.

## What changes

- `extras/claude-code` and `extras/codex` ship the hook in their plugins rather than in an opt-in `messaging-hooks.json`. A session that is in no group pays one CLI start and one daemon round trip per tool call, and sees nothing.
- The `Stop` hook (`wait --due` with `asyncRewake`) goes. It left a background process per session for up to a day (a_2pOTIVxnx), and it missed a turn that ended with Esc or an API error. Idle delivery stays with the doorbell, in every harness.
- Which posts the hook delivers mid-turn follows the urgency rules in a_2xhGMOtbP (the card on making immediate delivery the default). Until that lands, it delivers urgent posts only, since a normal post today waits for the agent to be idle.
- The daemon already stops ringing a pane whose hooks have run `muster msg` in the last five minutes. Check that rule still holds when every session carries the hook but most never read anything.
- `muster docs msg`, `extras/*/README.md` and `docs/configuration.md` describe the result.

## Before shipping

Measure the per-tool-call cost with `./dev --perf`. `muster --version` takes about 4 ms, so it is expected to be small, but the daemon round trip has not been measured.

## Not solved by this

An idle agent still has every doorbell failure: a draft in the prompt, a hidden pane, or one too short to show its prompt holds the wake. The `Stop` hook was the only fix for those. a_2izzXwq3v (a full-size terminal for reads and the doorbell) is the remaining answer.
title: Deliver messages to an agent at work through a plugin hook, not its prompt
